elements.text: Give urgent attention to the patient with suspected mpox and any of:

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with suspected mpox and any of:
elements.text: Shock1/systolic BP < 80

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with suspected mpox and any of:
elements.text: Thirst, dry mouth, poor skin turgor, BP < 90/60, dehydration likely

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with suspected mpox and any of:
elements.text: Unable to pass urine or stool

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with suspected mpox and any of:
elements.text: Respiratory rate ≥ 30, difficulty breathing at rest/while talking or oxygen saturation < 90%

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with suspected mpox and any of:
elements.text: Severe bleeding, pain, or discharge from the anus, proctitis likely

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with suspected mpox and any of:
elements.text: Foreskin retracted over glans and unable to reduce to normal position with swollen, painful glans, paraphimosis likely

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with suspected mpox and any of:
elements.text: Unable to swallow

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with suspected mpox and any of:
elements.text: Persistent nausea and vomiting

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with suspected mpox and any of:
elements.text: Chest pain, irregular pulse, swollen legs, myocarditis likely

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with suspected mpox and any of:
elements.text: Immunocompromised or at risk of severe disease: HIV not on ART/virologically unsuppressed, cancer, organ transplant, pregnant, diabetes, hypertension, chronic lung/ skin disease, obesity, age > 65

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with suspected mpox and any of:
elements.text: Eye lesion/s and vision changes, corneal infection likely

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with suspected mpox and any of:
elements.text: Decreased consciousness or confusion 18

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with suspected mpox and any of:
elements.text: Extensive skin lesions

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with suspected mpox and any of:
elements.text: Severe pain

elements.section: Manage and refer urgently:
elements.text: Manage and refer urgently:

elements.section: Manage and refer urgently:
elements.text: If oxygen saturation < 90%, give oxygen 1-4L/min via nasal prongs or 6-10L/min via facemask.

elements.section: Manage and refer urgently:
elements.text: If dehydration likely, give oral rehydration solution (ORS) and observe. Encourage small frequent sips. Aim for at least 1-2L in 2 hours. If unable to drink or shock/SBP < 80, give sodium chloride 0.9% 500mL IV over 30 minutes, repeat until SBP > 80. Continue 1L 6 hourly. Stop if breathing worsens.

elements.section: Manage and refer urgently:
elements.text: If severe pain, give morphine 5-10mg IM or diluted morphine 3-10mg slow IV2. Stop if BP drops < 90/60.

elements.section: Manage and refer urgently:
elements.text: If persistent nausea or vomiting, give single dose metoclopramide 10mg oral/IM/IV.

elements.section: Manage and refer urgently:
elements.text: If paraphimosis likely: if glans blue/black: refer urgently. If not, attempt manual reduction: wrap glans in gauze and apply increasing pressure for 10-15 minutes until foreskin can be replaced over glans. If unsuccessful, refer urgently.

elements.section: Manage and refer urgently:
elements.text: If unable to pass urine, insert urinary catheter.
MPOX: DIAGNOSIS AND MANAGEMENT

1If SBP < 80, pulse ≥ 100, respiratory rate > 30, confusion/restlessness, weakness, shock likely. 2Dilute 10mg morphine with 9mL sodium chloride 0.9%. Start with 3mL IV over 3 minutes. If needed, give another 1mL/minute until pain improved, up to 10mL.
If unsure, discuss with National Institute for Communicable Diseases (NICD) hotline on 0800 212 552. Continue to manage the patient with suspected mpox 41

Approach to the patient with suspected mpox not needing urgent attention • If status unknown, test for HIV 124. Also send blood for syphilis serology and review result within 7 days 66. • Ask about anal 61 and genital symptoms 62. If patient has anal sex and anal bleeding/pain/discharge, proctitis likely 61. • If rash or lesions all look similar and change or progress at a similar pace (figure 1), mpox is more likely. • Look for other cause of rash/lesions according to the distribution of rash/lesions and presence or absence of itchiness:
Generalised rash or lesion/s

Itchy • If crops of vesicles at different stages of healing and no swollen lymph nodes, chickenpox likely. • If advanced HIV disease and hyperpigmented papules, papular pruritic eruption likely 84. • If burrows in web spaces or skin folds and itch worse at night, scabies likely 84. • If new medication in past 3 months, drug-induced rash likely 88.

Non-itchy • If conjunctivitis, cough, runny nose and flat red rash spreading from face to body, measles likely. Notify. • If tick bite or eschar (small dark scab) and rash spreading from extremities to body, tick bite fever likely 38.

Non-itchy • If firm, dome-shaped papules with central dimple, molluscum contagiosum likely 89. • If painful, grouped vesicles on red base especially around mouth 52 or genitals, herpes simplex likely 65. • If painful vesicles around mouth and on palms and soles, hand-foot and mouth disease likely. • If painful blisters in a band on one side of body, shingles likely 83.
Itchy If honey- coloured crusts
especially around mouth
and nose, impetigo likely
Localised rash or lesion/s

• Suspect mpox if patient is a contact of a probable/confirmed mpox case in the 21 days before symptom onset, or presents with new unexplained lesion/s of the skin (face, palms of hands/soles of feet, genitals, anus, rectum, mouth or eyes) and any of: headache, temperature > 38.5°C in the last 2 days, sore throat/nasal congestion/ cough, swollen lymph nodes, body pain/muscle aches, backache, severe weakness/tiredness. • While looking for other cause of rash/lesions/symptoms: wear N95/FFP2 mask, gloves, gown and eye protection. If possible, isolate patient and provide surgical mask. Source: Mayo Clinic and WHO
